title: Invited: EDA for Heterogeneous Integration
problem: Heterogeneous integration (chiplet-based systems) demands new EDA methodologies beyond traditional monolithic chip design. Chiplet disaggregation, multi-physics analysis, physical design for substrates, and interchiplet communication optimization remain open challenges.
motivation: Chiplet-based design offers cost, yield, and thermal benefits but introduces unprecedented complexity in system partitioning, design space exploration, and verification. Traditional EDA tools are insufficient for cross-chiplet optimization.
method: The paper describes how to automate design of multi-chip systems in four stages: first, deciding which parts of a design go on which chiplet and optimizing their interactions; second, verifying the designs with fast machine-learning models early in design and detailed physics simulations (analyzing heat and mechanical stress) before release; third, physically placing chiplets on a substrate, routing connections between them, and managing power distribution; fourth, providing reusable chiplet designs, standard file formats, and shared specifications. Together, these methods address the complete flow of multi-chip system design.
key_novelty: The paper identifies what comprehensive automated-design capabilities are needed for multi-chip systems, spanning from how designs partition across chips to their physical arrangement.
contributions: Taxonomy of four core EDA challenges for chiplet-based systems
Integration of system-technology co-optimization with chiplet disaggregation strategies
Multiphysics simulation from ML-driven early-stage to signoff-quality analysis
Infrastructure requirements for chiplet libraries and standardized design formats
limitations: Invited position paper; specific algorithmic or tool implementations not presented.
primary_theme: EDA methodology framework for chiplet-based heterogeneous system design
